title: Global generation on a separably closed point
statement:
If $K$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed], every abelian sheaf $F$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] on
$\Spec(K)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] is generated by its global sections in the sense of
[def-kun-global-generated].

proof.text: A separably closed field K, viewed as the local ring of Spec(K) at its unique point, is strictly henselian: the maximal ideal is zero, the henselian idempotent-lifting condition is immediate for the pair (K,0), and the residue field is K itself. Therefore the existing strictly-henselian sections-to-stalk theorem [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk], specialized to R=K and the chosen geometric point, gives a natural isomorphism $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}(K)_{\mathrm{Et}},F)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar t}$ for every geometric point $\bar t$ of $\operatorname{Spec}K$.

source.place: Tag 03QO (lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian), global-sections/stalk comparison; specialization to Spec K

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and let $\epsilon:\bigoplus_{s\in\Gamma(S_{\mathrm{Et}},F)}\underline{\mathbf Z}\to F$ be the evaluation morphism of [def-kun-global-generated]. Given $a\in F_{\bar t}$, the germ isomorphism of step 1 gives $s\in F(S)$ with $s_{\bar t}=a$. Let $\iota_s$ be the coproduct inclusion of the summand indexed by $s$, and let $1$ be the canonical global section of that constant integer sheaf. By the defining formula for evaluation, $\epsilon_S((\iota_s)_S(1))=s$. Taking germs [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] gives $\epsilon_{\bar t}(((\iota_s)_S(1))_{\bar t})=s_{\bar t}=a$. Thus $\epsilon_{\bar t}$ is surjective. This uses only the canonical sections and naturality of a sheaf morphism, without identifying the entire stalk of the coproduct.

The evaluation morphism is therefore surjective on every geometric stalk. By the existing stalkwise criterion [lem-kun-global-generated-stalkwise], this is equivalent to the evaluation morphism being an epimorphism; by the definition [def-kun-global-generated], $F$ is globally generated.
